profileSetup.accessibilityNoticeText: We use these settings to score the accessibility of every route for your profile, using OpenStreetMap data: steps without a ramp (the route is shown as not accessible), raised kerbs, cobblestone, wheelchair access at the stops, benches to rest on and route length, depending on the profile. Where the profile has a distance limit, longer routes are not listed.

aiRoutes.confirmMessage: A new route will be created with AI from places near you and added to the route list. This may take a few seconds.
aiRoutes.errorNoPlaces: There are not enough places near you to build a route. Try again from somewhere more central.

aiRoutes.errorGeneric: Something went wrong while creating your route. Please try again.
aiRoutes.explainBody:
The routes in this list are curated: their stops, the order of the stops, the title and the description were chosen in advance. No language model wrote them.

“Create a route with AI” is the only AI feature here. It asks a language model to pick places near you, put them in order, and write the title and description. Routes made this way carry an AI badge.

For every route, curated or AI, the rest is computed, not guessed: OSRM builds the real pedestrian path, which gives the distance and timings, and the accessibility scorer checks it against OpenStreetMap and Wheelmap data for your mobility profile.

The model never decides whether a place or a route is accessible, and it can only choose from places that already exist in the map data.
